properties.name: FIELD CONFIRMATION (flo2, 2026-09-14): "import materialises schema defaults the export left implicit — 853 of reflow2's 26,795 edges gained a field; converges after one pass; a CI gate comparing hashes fires falsely once per rehydrate" — the 853 are reflow2's AUTHORED_BY edges and the field is `roles`: the one-time migration #505 shipped, seen from the consumer's side, not a new defect; the class it belongs to is the 2026-08-24 finding that the committed export is not in its importer's normal form
properties.statement:
RELAYED by Anthony from the flo2 session, 2026-09-14, in its words: "Import materialises schema defaults the export left implicit — 853 of reflow2's 26,795 edges gained a field. Nothing lost, and it converges after exactly one pass. But the first export after a rehydrate differs from the last one before it with zero user activity. A CI design gate comparing hashes fires falsely once per rehydrate. Normalise on ingest, store that as the baseline — trivial if you know, alarming if you don't."

IDENTIFIED, by measurement on reflow2's own export the same day: this export holds exactly 853 AUTHORED_BY edges and every one carries `roles`; 0 carry the legacy single `role`. PR #505 (merged 2026-09-14) made AUTHORED_BY's stored shape the set `roles`, and its importer and every on-disk open rewrite legacy edges to that shape (graph.rs migrate_authored_by_roles). flo2 rehydrated from an export written BEFORE #505, the import migrated all 853 edges, and its next export differed from the document by exactly those 853 — once, then a fixed point. That is the migration doing what it was built to do, and it was announced in the CHANGELOG ("legacy edges read right and migrate; import_graph normalises a consumer's older export on the way in, so one design never holds both shapes"). It is not a schema default and there is nothing to fix in the migration.

THE CLASS IS REAL AND ALREADY ON THE RECORD, twice: fact:defect-import-materialises-defaults-so-a-restored-graph-reads-as-changed (2026-08-15, Artifact.granularity/volatility — settled by dec:the-safe-reading-lives-in-the-reader-not-the-store, which removed those two defaults from the schema) and fact:export-import-export-is-lossless-but-not-a-fixed-point-until-one-normalising-pass (2026-08-24, REALIZES.conformance null→unchecked on 223 legacy edges — "either the EXPORTER stops omitting the default, or the IMPORTER stops materialising it, and the two sides currently disagree"). Measured today on reflow2's own export: 0 of 497 REALIZES edges lack conformance, 0 of 280 ALLOCATED_TO lack weight_basis, 0 of 66 SCHEDULED_FOR lack modality, 0 node or edge schema defaults are declared any more — so reflow2's own document IS in normal form now; a consumer's older document may not be, and a MIGRATION (roles) will always produce exactly one such pass by design.

WHAT FLO2'S FRAMING ADDS, and it is the part worth keeping: the cost is not the diff, it is that nothing SAYS what the diff is. "The first export after a rehydrate differs with zero user activity" and the gate reads that as the design having changed. The 08-15 report said the same: the honest fix (re-export, commit) is indistinguishable from the dishonest one (--no-verify) unless somebody diffs property by property. Their proposal — normalise on ingest and store that as the baseline — is one direction of the 08-24 finding; for a migration the importer MUST rewrite, so the remaining honest move is to SAY SO: import and open report what they migrated (count, edge type, field), and the hash gate's message names a migration on open or import as a benign cause with its recipe (re-export once, commit, done). Not chosen here; Anthony's call.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether flo2's gate was reflow2_check's lineage/behind check or a hash comparison of their own; whether any consumer document still carries the 2026-08-24 REALIZES shape (the flo2 number says roles, not conformance).
